name: Progressive Cone Dystrophy

criteria.description: Progressive loss of central visual acuity
Dyschromatopsia predominantly affecting red-green color discrimination
Reduced or absent cone responses on electroretinogram (ERG) with preserved rod responses
Macular atrophy or pigmentary changes observed on fundoscopic examination
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive central visual acuity loss, color vision deficiency, and characteristic ERG findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

imaging: Fundus photography showing macular atrophy and pigmentary changes
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealing photoreceptor layer thinning in the macula
other: Electroretinogram (ERG) demonstrating reduced cone responses with preserved rod function

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant rod photoreceptor degeneration with night blindness
Peripheral visual field loss precedes central vision loss
Congenital absence of cone function with nystagmus from infancy
Complete color blindness without progressive visual acuity loss

redFlags: Rapidly progressive vision loss over weeks
Presence of optic disc swelling or hemorrhages
Associated systemic neurological symptoms such as ataxia or cognitive decline
references: Hamel C. Cone rod dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:7.
Michaelides M, Hardcastle AJ, Hunt DM, Moore AT. Progressive cone and cone-rod dystrophies: phenotypes and underlying molecular genetic basis. Surv Ophthalmol. 2006;51(3):232-258.
